name: Risk Balanced
description: Spreads exposure across different risk drivers — growth, rates, inflation, and a small convex sleeve — rather than across tickers that all secretly depend on the same driver. Complexity here has to earn its keep against core-index.

sleeves.name: Growth equity
sleeves.rationale: Exposure to the economy expanding. Sized down from a classic 60/40 because the other sleeves are doing work a bond-only ballast cannot.

sleeves.name: Long duration
sleeves.rationale: Exposure to falling rates and deflationary shocks. Historically negatively correlated with equity in growth scares — but that relationship broke in 2022, which is exactly the kind of assumption the backtest should be stress-testing.

sleeves.name: Real assets
sleeves.rationale: Inflation and monetary-debasement hedge. The sleeve most likely to look like dead weight for years and then justify itself in a single window.

sleeves.name: Convex sleeve
sleeves.rationale: Small, deliberately sized so a total loss is survivable and irrelevant to the plan. Position sizing is the entire risk control here — not conviction, not a thesis.

sleeves.name: Cash buffer
sleeves.rationale: Dry powder and drawdown insurance. Also the sleeve that funds rebalancing into whatever just fell.
